items.rationale: The confirmed supply-line burst is insured under 2.4.2–2.4.3. The €530 assessment estimate is below the separate €3,000 cap in 5.2.6(b); the €500 deductible applies once to the event, not to each line.
Indoor leak location is covered under 5.2.6(a). The €567 estimate plus €254 for technician time totals €821, below the shared €1,000 cap.
On-site leak-location time is covered under 5.2.6(a). The 2.5 hours are estimated at €254 gross, and the combined €821 with line 2 is below the €1,000 cap.
This is the first vehicle charge on the leak-detection invoice. Under 5.2.6(c), the €70 net cap is €83.30 gross at 19% VAT.

Sections 5.1(b) and 5.2.2 cover necessary protection of property during reinstatement, but the invoice does not identify what the fleece protected. If it protected a necessary access route or retained finishes, 25 m² at about €3.50/m² is €87.50.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a), (d) cover removal of the damaged flooring and associated skirting that cannot be refitted. Estimate 82.8 m² at €14/m², including transport to the container but not final disposal.
Necessary substrate preparation on the affected floor is covered under 7.1.7(b) and is distinct from lifting the linoleum. Estimate 82.8 m² at €7/m².
Disposal of insured flooring debris is covered under 5.2.1 at an estimated €60. Line 17 duplicates it under 7.1.8(c), so only the lower charge is payable, or this first charge if equal.

Section 7.1.7(b) allows separate drying-equipment labour, but 7.1.8(b)–(c) excludes overhead and duplicate labour. If these two hours represent distinct on-site support rather than work already billed in line 14, allow about €55/hour.

items.description: Dust protection including materials and labour
items.rationale: Necessary dust barriers protecting retained property during repairs are covered under 5.2.2 if distinct from the fleece floor protection. Estimate 10 m² at €9/m² including materials and labour.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(e) require contact with escaping water; the separate kitchen stayed dry. The conditional estimate for 25 m² at €5/m² is €125.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) allow drying of wetted screed and adjoining areas beyond the 82.8 m² stripped, but not the dry kitchen. If moisture records support the billed 121.9 m², a large-area rate of €12/m² gives €1,462.80, including utilities.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(b) cover drying wetted cavities where it is a distinct measure from large-area floor drying. Allow about €340 gross for one cavity-drying setup.

Section 7.1.7(b) expressly permits separate labour for installing, monitoring and removing drying equipment. The benchmark for four skilled hours is €349 gross, provided the same work is not also paid under line 9.
The first drying-contractor vehicle charge is admissible for repair under 5.2.6(c), capped at €70 net × 1.19 = €83.30 gross.
Section 5.2.6(c) excludes the second vehicle charge on the same contractor invoice. The conditional estimate is €83.30, the gross ceiling for an eligible first trip.
The claim identifies this as the same disposal billed on line 8. Under 7.1.8(c), this later charge is payable only if it is lower than line 8; the conditional disposal benchmark is €60.
